topIssues.title: ZKDisputeGame: Handle address(0) bond credit claiming via monitoring or contract change
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Context

In `ZKDisputeGame`, when a parent game resolves as `CHALLENGER_WINS` and the child was never challenged, `claimData.challenger` is `address(0)`. The `resolve()` function assigns `totalBonds` to `normalModeCredit[address(0)]` — the bond is effectively "burned" by crediting the zero address.

However, nobody will call `claimCredit(address(0))` to actually move the funds through the DelayedWETH two-phase withdrawal, so the ETH remains stranded in DelayedWETH indefinitely.

This was identified during review of ethereum-optimism/optimism#19606:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19606#discussion_r2972200379

## Options Discussed

1. **Monitoring approach (current plan):** Update monitoring to account for the fact that `address(0)` credits will never be claimed, so they don't show up as anomalies. The ETH stays in DelayedWETH — monitoring just needs to understand this is expected.

2. **Contract-level approach:** Piggyback on other `claimCredit()` calls to automatically process `address(0)` credit at the same time. Downside: makes the code messier.

3. **Automatic burn in `resolve()`:** Not feasible due to DelayedWETH's two-phase withdrawal — both phases can't happen in a single transaction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide on approach (monitoring adjustment vs contract change)
- [ ] If monitoring: update `dispute-mon` to expect that `address(0)` credit in ZK games is never claimed, so it doesn't flag as an anomaly
- [ ] If contract: implement and test the piggyback approach in `ZKDisputeGame`
- [ ] Ensure monitoring correctly accounts for ETH held in DelayedWETH from ZK game bond burns

## Related

- ethereum-optimism/optimism#18424 — broader ZK game monitoring issue
- ethereum-optimism/optimism#19606 — ZKDisputeGame implementation PR where this was identified

topPRs.title: pure: add pure derivation pipeline in op-core/pure
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds `op-core/pure/` package implementing a pure function derivation pipeline
- `PureDerive()` takes L1 data + safe head state, returns derived L2 payload attributes — no I/O, no L2 state reads
- Post-Holocene only, with protocol modification: no overlapping span batches (eliminates L2 fetcher dependency)

## Design

Single pure function that loops over L1 blocks sequentially:
1. Apply system config updates from L1 receipts
2. Parse frames from batcher transactions
3. Assemble channels (Holocene single-channel strict-order model)
4. Decode and validate batches
5. Build payload attributes (L1 info deposit + user deposits + batch txs)
6. Generate empty batches when sequencer window expires

Reuses existing pure functions from `op-node/rollup/derive/` (frame parsing, channel assembly, batch decoding, deposit encoding, L1 block info). Fresh implementation for the orchestration layer.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `types.go` | L1Input, DerivedBlock, l2Cursor, BlockInfo adapter |
| `channels.go` | Holocene single-channel assembler |
| `batches.go` | Batch decoding, validation, empty batch generation |
| `attributes.go` | PayloadAttributes assembly |
| `derive.go` | `PureDerive()` entry point |
| `helpers_test.go` | Shared test utilities |

## Test plan

- [x] 31 unit tests covering all pipeline stages
- [x] Channel assembly: single-frame, multi-frame, new channel discards old, timeout, out-of-order
- [x] Batch validation: correct timestamp, wrong timestamp, epoch range, overlap rejection
- [x] Empty batch generation: window expiry detection, correct epoch advancement
- [x] Attributes assembly: epoch boundaries, same epoch, Holocene-specific fields
- [x] End-to-end: single batch, empty epochs, multiple channels/epochs, channel timeout, invalid batch skip
- [ ] Differential test against existing pipeline (follow-up)

topPRs.title: test(alloy-op-evm): cover SDM post-exec settlement conservation
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
## Description

Adds unit coverage for the SDM post-exec **fee settlement** — the per-recipient balance changes applied when a refund fires (sender credit + beneficiary / base-fee-vault / operator-fee-vault debits). This path was previously only exercised indirectly (the producer/verifier roundtrip runs at base fee 0, so all settlement deltas were zero), leaving the economic correctness unasserted.

## Tests added (`rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/tests.rs`, `mod sdm`)

- **`test_post_exec_settlement_deltas_conserve_value`** — pins each per-recipient share against the spec formula (`base = refund × basefee`, `beneficiary = refund × (effective_gas_price − basefee)`, operator-fee debit `> 0` post-Isthmus) and asserts the **sender credit equals the sum of the three debits** — the ETH-supply-conservation / "no infinite mint" invariant.
- **`test_post_exec_settlement_deltas_skip_non_refunding_txs`** — deposits, the post-exec (`0x7D`) tx itself, and zero-refund txs produce no settlement.
- **`test_post_exec_settlement_underflow_is_rejected`** — a debit exceeding a recipient's balance fails with `PostExecSettlementUnderflow` rather than saturating.

## Supporting change

Threads a `base_fee` parameter through the test-only `build_executor` / `SDMExecutorFixture` (defaults to `0`, so existing tests are unchanged) — a non-zero base fee is required for the settlement deltas to be non-trivial.

## Notes

These close the two items called out by name in the SDM test-hardening ticket (#21324): the ETH-supply-conservation test and the `PostExecSettlementUnderflow` path. Test-only change; no production code touched.

## Verification

- New tests pass; full `alloy-op-evm` lib suite green (56 → 59).
- Formatted with the pinned nightly rustfmt (`just fmt-check` recipe).
